extracted.intended_audience: IP attorneys, law firm administrators, AIPLA members, and researchers analyzing IP practice economics
extracted.subtask_description: AIPLA Economic Survey report pages listing firm-level demographic and operational metrics for IP/practice-focused law firms (counts by attorney roles, gender, ethnicity; office locations; remote work; space plans). Primarily tabular survey results broken down by firm size and geography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of Attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of attorneys in the firm (size categories shown: One, Two, 3-5, 6-10, 11-30, 31-100, 101 or More).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as number of firms reporting and percent distribution across size categories; used as a primary stratifier for other tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of Major Office Locations
rubrics_metrics.description: How many major office locations (staffed by two or more partners) the firm had in 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tabulated by firm size (Q3); shows number of firms reporting, mean (average) number of major locations, and breakdown by firm-size bins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent of Practice That is IP
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorization of firms by percent of their practice devoted to IP (e.g., 75% or More vs Less than 75%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a column/stratifier in tables to compare firm characteristics by degree of IP focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position of the Person Responding on Behalf of the Firm (Q1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Role/title of the survey respondent (examples shown: Managing Partner/Shareholder, Administrator/Other Position).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as percent distribution across response categories and stratified by firm-size and other groupings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firm plan to close major office locations (Q4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the firm plans to close any major office locations in 2023 or 2024 (responses: Yes / No / Not Sure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tabulated by firm-size and other stratifiers with percent distributions and counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in office space leased or owned (Q5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the firm anticipates changing or has changed the amount of office space it leases or owns (responses: Reduce office space / Increase office space / No changes planned / Don't Know/Not Sure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percent and count breakdowns shown by firm size and other categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentage of Employees Working Remotely (Q6A-B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of employees that worked remotely in 2022 and percentage that will work remotely in 2023 (means reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as mean (average) percent and number of firms reporting, broken down by firm-size categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solo practitioner status (Q8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the responding firm/person is a solo practitioner (Yes / No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shown as percent distribution and counts across firm-size and geographic categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of attorneys by role (Q9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of attorneys in 2022 by role categories: Equity Partner/Shareholder, Partner-track attorney, Non-partner track attorney, Of Counsel, Contract/Part-time, and Total Attorneys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables provide number of firms reporting, mean, first quartile, median, third quartile, and stratification by firm-size bins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of IP Equity Partners/Shareholders by gender (Q10A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of IP equity partners/shareholders in the firm in 2022 broken out by gender (Male, Female, Other, Total).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented with number of firms reporting and summary statistics (mean, quartiles) by firm-size categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of IP Partner-track attorneys by gender (Q10B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of IP partner-track attorneys in the firm in 2022 broken out by gender (Male, Female, Other, Total).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes number of firms reporting and summary statistics (means, quartiles) stratified by firm-size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of IP Non-partner track attorneys by gender (Q10C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of IP non-partner track attorneys in the firm in 2022 broken out by gender (Male, Female, Other, Total).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported with summary statistics and stratified by firm-size bins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of IP Of Counsel (or equivalent) by gender (Q10D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of IP Of Counsel (or equivalent) by gender in the firm in 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables include number of firms reporting and distributional statistics by firm-size categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of IP Contract/Part-time professionals by gender (Q10E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of contract/part-time IP professionals by gender in the firm in 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes mean, quartiles, and breakdowns by firm-size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of USPTO-registered Patent Agents (not attorneys) by gender (Q10F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of USPTO-registered patent agents (non-attorney) in the firm in 2022 broken out by gender and firm-size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides number of firms reporting, mean, quartiles, and stratification by firm-size bins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of IP Technical Advisors/Assistants, including Searchers by gender (Q10G)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of technical advisors/assistants (including searchers) in the firm in 2022 by gender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented with summary statistics and firm-size stratification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of IP Paralegal/Legal Assistants (billable support staff) by gender (Q10H)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of IP paralegals/legal assistants (billable support staff) by gender in the firm in 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables show number of firms reporting, mean, quartiles, medians, and breakdowns by firm-size and geography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of IP Equity Partners/Shareholders by ethnicity (Q10I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of IP equity partners/shareholders in 2022 broken out by ethnicity categories (White/Caucasian, Black/African American, Hispanic/Latino, Asian/Pacific Islander, N. American Indian/Native Canadian, Mixed Race, Other, Total).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported with number of firms reporting and distributional statistics across firm-size bins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of IP Partner-track attorneys by ethnicity (Q10J)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of partner-track IP attorneys in 2022 broken out by ethnicity categories (same categories as Q10I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes means, quartiles, and stratification by firm-size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of IP Non-partner track attorneys by ethnicity (Q10K)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of non-partner-track IP attorneys in 2022 broken out by ethnicity categories (White, Black, Hispanic, Asian, Native American, Mixed Race, Other, Total).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented with summary statistics and firm-size stratification (table continues beyond chunk).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic / CMSA location stratifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographic columns used to stratify results (examples: Boston CMSA, NYC CMSA, Philadelphia CMSA, Washington DC CMSA, Other East, Metro Southeast, Other Southeast, Chicago CMSA, Minneapolis–St. Paul PMSA, Other Central, Texas, Los Angeles CMSA, San Francisco CMSA, Other West).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most tables include geographic stratification columns to compare responses across metro areas/regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabular summary statistics reported
rubrics_metrics.description: For count metrics the report provides summary statistics (Number of Firms Reporting, Mean (Average), First Quartile (25%), Median, Third Quartile (75%)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These distributional statistics are provided for many numeric items (attorney counts, staffing counts, etc.) to convey central tendency and spread across reporting firms.
